title: Environment Management
summary: Environment is our surroundings: all forms of life, air, water, land, buildings and vehicles. Environmental degradation is an unfavourable change of our surroundings (land, water and air degradation). Causes: (1) uncontrolled population growth (more demand for food, fuel, space and jobs leading to industrialisation, urbanisation, deforestation, construction, slums, unhygienic living; delay the first child and marry only at the legal age: 18 for girls, 21 for boys); (2) technical advancement (industries, mines, automobiles and aeroplanes release toxic chemical wastes, harmful gases and radioactive pollutants and deplete the ozone layer); (3) poor agricultural practices (overgrazing, excessive chemical fertilisers and pesticides, shifting cultivation, over-ploughing and overcropping cause soil hardening and erosion); (4) improper personal habits (spitting, open defecation, bathing and washing near water sources, smoking, loud music); (5) natural causes (earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, floods, famine and strong winds).

Soil degradation: chemical fertilisers, pesticides and industrial wastes kill soil micro-organisms (the 'farmer's friends' that decompose waste), reducing fertility; pesticides enter food chains causing cancer and nervous disorders; deforestation exposes soil, causing erosion. Deforestation: loss of wood and medicines, oxygen (forests are 'oxygen banks'), rainfall and water recharge; leads to landslides, floods, soil erosion, climate change, drying of lakes and rivers and extinction of wildlife. Air degradation: acid rain (sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides forming dilute acids; erosion and discolouration of the Taj Mahal's marble), ozone layer depletion (harmful gases from refrigerators and fire extinguishers; skin cancer, cataract, stunted plants), global warming (CO2 and methane trap radiation like a blanket; hotter summers, less cold winters, unpredictable rain), man-made disasters (Hiroshima and Nagasaki, Gulf War oil fires, Bhopal gas tragedy, Chernobyl radioactive leakage) and respiratory diseases (bronchitis, asthma). Water degradation: foam cuts oxygen to aquatic life; sewage causes jaundice, diarrhoea, dysentery, typhoid and malaria; industrial wastes cause leukaemia, cancer and allergies. Slum conditions: overcrowding, no sanitation, jaundice, TB, scabies, plague and loud noise leading to deafness and stress.

Eco-friendly (bio-friendly) means not harmful to the environment in production, use and disposal. Biodegradable items decompose; recycled ones are reused. Non-eco-friendly vs eco-friendly: leaded petrol vs unleaded petrol; crude motor oil vs double refined oil; synthetic paints vs water-based paints; nylon and acrylic fabrics vs jute and cotton; polythene bags vs paper bags; traditional chullahs vs smokeless chullahs, solar cookers and biogas; thermocol glasses vs earthen cups. The Eco Mark (launched February 1991 by the Ministry of Environment and Forests; given by the BIS; an ISI mark with an earthen pot) certifies minimum pollution standards. Eco-friendly practices: household waste made into compost manure (as the Tihar Jail inmates do), recycling paper, textiles, metal, glass and plastics, sewage treatment plants for industrial wastes, separating pollutants from gases, 'Sulabh Shauchalayas' and afforestation.
## What we and the government can do

Individuals: the 3 R's (reduce, reuse, recycle), solar cookers and heaters, hygiene, proper disposal, family planning, saving water, avoiding loudspeakers and smoking, living near the workplace, car sharing, unleaded petrol or CNG, cycling and public transport, planting trees, reporting illegal felling and spreading awareness. Government: locating industries away from cities, strict pollution laws for industries and vehicles, waste treatment plants, linking industries to reuse each other's waste, family planning, domestic waste disposal (sanitary refill: municipal waste dumped in an enclosed area and covered with soil), public education, promoting biogas and solar devices, healthy farm practices (natural manures, crop rotation, mixed cropping), tree planting and wildlife reserves.

Name the practices that cause air degradation and the one that causes land degradation. Choose from smoking, spitting, loud music, open defecation.

vsa: How does technical advancement contribute to environmental degradation?
Industries, mines and vehicles release toxic wastes, harmful gases and radioactive pollutants. These deplete the ozone layer and kill life in air, water and land.
Ramesh wants to dispose of dry leaves and kitchen waste from his garden in an eco-friendly way. Which practice should he adopt and what is one benefit?
He should make compost in a compost pit. The compost is a manure that increases soil fertility and saves on chemical fertilisers.
What do you understand by 'environmental degradation'? Mention its three natural causes.
It is an unfavourable change of our surroundings. Natural causes are earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and floods (also famine and strong winds).
Forests supply oxygen, influence rainfall and temperature, and prevent soil erosion. They also recharge water sources and shelter wildlife.
Name any two effects of the depletion of the ozone layer.
More ultraviolet rays reach the earth, causing skin cancer and eye problems like cataract. They also stunt the growth of plants.
What is 'eco friendly'? Give two examples.
Products and practices not harmful to the environment in production, use and disposal. Paper bags and unleaded petrol are examples.
sa: Explain the causes of environmental degradation (any three).

(i) Uncontrolled population growth increases demand for food, fuel and space and leads to deforestation and slums. (ii) Technical advancement releases toxic wastes and harmful gases. (iii) Poor agricultural practices and improper personal habits degrade soil, water and air.
Explain the effects of deforestation (three points).
(i) Landslides, floods and soil erosion. (ii) No rainfall and drying of springs, lakes and rivers, changing the climate. (iii) Extinction of wildlife and reduced availability of land.
How can an individual help in environmental conservation? (three points)

(i) Follow the 3 R's of reduce, reuse and recycle and use solar cookers. (ii) Use public transport or share cars and plant a tree. (iii) Keep the family small, save water and avoid smoking and loud speakers.
Explain the role of the government in controlling environmental degradation (three points).

(i) Enforce strict pollution control laws and ensure waste treatment plants in industries. (ii) Provide efficient waste disposal and promote biogas and solar devices. (iii) Educate people, promote healthy farm practices and tree planting, and conserve wildlife.
la: Explain the effects of air and water degradation on human life.

(i) Air: acid rain damages plants, animals and monuments like the Taj Mahal. (ii) The ozone layer is depleted, causing skin cancer and eye problems. (iii) Global warming raises temperature and makes rainfall unpredictable. (iv) Man-made disasters such as Bhopal and Chernobyl kill and harm life. (v) Water: sewage causes jaundice, diarrhoea, typhoid and malaria. (vi) Industrial wastes cause cancer, leukaemia and allergies and foam cuts oxygen for aquatic life.
